Title: Narrative is the recurrent first-visible point of pipeline drift — focus trials and controls there
Description: The report shows the Narrative stage is the most frequent earliest observable break in the requested company-first editorial hierarchy. Treating Narrative as a primary locus for diagnostic intervention (instead of only changing Idea or Compose) offers the clearest, source-supported opportunity to preserve a company-first introduction while keeping product details as supporting context.
Audience: Content experiment designers, prompt engineers, editorial leads and workflow owners running Nuëyon.Compose pipeline experiments.
Rationale: Why it matters: Experiment traceability across 007–009 repeatedly localizes first visible hierarchy shifts to Narrative (e.g., 007 runs 001–002; 008 A-002; 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003). The same experiments also show that a company-first Idea can be selected yet be reframed downstream, so upstream Idea changes alone are insufficient. Focusing a controlled trial on Narrative (with fixed upstream inputs) minimizes confounding sources and directly tests whether Narrative-stage conditioning or prompt wording is allowing product- or orchestration-led reframing. Gaps & uncertainty: Narrative is the most recurrent visible locus but not the sole origin — some runs start in Idea or Synthesis — so a Narrative-only fix may not address all failure modes.
Evidence: Executive findings and 'First observable drift by run' tables: the report states 'Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift' and lists concrete runs where Narrative is first (Experiment 007 candidates 001–002; Experiment 008 A-002; Experiment 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003). It also records runs where Idea or Synthesis initiated drift (e.g., 008 A-001, 007 candidate 003), supporting the qualification that Narrative is recurrent but not sole.
